title: Complete Reference: estimate_concentration_field()
text: Spatial transcriptomics data gives us discrete transcript cell locations, many biological processes — ligand gradients, cytokine fields, metabolite concentrations — continuous. estimate_concentration_field() bridges gap computing steady-state concentration field set point sources (mRNA transcripts, detected proteins) produce physically motivated diffusion-clearance model. result dense concentration map tissue, interpolated point source locations. can used : Identify signalling molecule concentrated Compute concentration seen cell Create two-gene ratio maps (spatial domains ligand/receptor balance) Visualise diffusion length affects signal range

title: Complete Reference: estimate_concentration_field()
text: function solves screened Poisson equation (steady-state diffusion-clearance PDE): D∇2C(𝐱)−λC(𝐱)+s(𝐱)=0D \nabla^2 C(\mathbf{x}) - \lambda C(\mathbf{x}) + s(\mathbf{x}) = 0 key derived quantity diffusion length: L=D/λL = \sqrt{D / \lambda} LL sets characteristic distance concentration decays point source. single important parameter tune. shape field depends LL; amplitude scales 1/D1/D. Practical interpretation: LL roughly radius influence single transcript. distance r≫Lr \gg L source, concentration negligible. r≪Lr \ll L, concentration near maximum.

what: Section 1 – Synthetic tissue and transcript layout
title: Complete Reference: estimate_concentration_field()
text: kidney-bean-shaped tissue two synthetic genes: Gene : focal cluster upper-left, plus sparse background. High UMI count. Gene B: 500 transcripts right-biased spatial distribution. Low UMI count.
code: in_kidney <- function(x, y, oa = 9, ob = 7, ncx = 5, nr = 3.8)   (x/oa)^2 + (y/ob)^2 < 1 & sqrt((x - ncx)^2 + y^2) >= nr  cands      <- data.frame(x = runif(18000, -11, 11), y = runif(18000, -9, 9)) tissue_pts <- cands[in_kidney(cands$x, cands$y), ][1:3000, ]  if (requireNamespace("TissueMask", quietly = TRUE)) {   tissue_mask <- TissueMask::fit_spatial_mask(     tissue_pts, method = "raster",     raster_resolution = 256L, raster_sigma = 0.7, raster_threshold = 0.15,     verbose = FALSE) } else {   pts_sf      <- st_as_sf(tissue_pts, coords = c("x","y"))   tissue_mask <- st_convex_hull(st_union(pts_sf)) } mu_t <- sf::st_union(tissue_mask) # Gene A: focal cluster at (-4.5, 3.8) + sparse background tc_A_cl <- data.frame(x = rnorm(350, -4.5, 1.2), y = rnorm(350, 3.8, 0.9)) A_in    <- as.logical(sf::st_within(   sf::st_as_sf(tc_A_cl, coords = c("x","y")), mu_t, sparse = FALSE)[, 1L]) tc_A_cl <- tc_A_cl[A_in, ] tc_A_sc <- sample_in_mask(tissue_mask, 50) tc_A    <- rbind(tc_A_cl, tc_A_sc) tc_A$umi <- c(rpois(nrow(tc_A_cl), 15), rpois(nrow(tc_A_sc), 2))  # Gene B: right-biased random distribution tc_B_all <- sample_in_mask(tissue_mask, 2000) prob_B   <- plogis(tc_B_all$x / 3) tc_B     <- tc_B_all[runif(nrow(tc_B_all)) < prob_B, ][1:500, ] tc_B$umi <- rpois(nrow(tc_B), 5) tissue_sf <- sf::st_sf(geometry = tissue_mask)  ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = tissue_sf, fill = "grey92", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4) +   geom_point(data = tc_A, aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Gene A", size = log1p(umi)),              alpha = 0.6) +   geom_point(data = tc_B, aes(x = x, y = y, color = "Gene B", size = log1p(umi)),              alpha = 0.5) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("Gene A" = "#e74c3c", "Gene B" = "#2980b9"),                      name = NULL) +   scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.3, 2.5), name = "log(UMI+1)") +   coord_sf(datum = NA) + theme_demo() +   labs(title    = "Section 1: Synthetic kidney-bean tissue",        subtitle = "Gene A: focal upper-left | Gene B: broad right-biased",        x = "X", y = "Y")

title: Getting Started with TissueField
text: Spatial transcriptomics gives us discrete detections: list (x, y) coordinates individual mRNA molecules found. many biological processes operate continuous gradients — ligand concentrations, cytokine fields, metabolite distributions. TissueField bridges gap. Given set transcript coordinates tissue mask polygon, estimate_concentration_field() computes steady-state concentration transcripts produce diffusing point sources inside tissue: D∇2C(𝐱)−λC(𝐱)+s(𝐱)=0D \nabla^2 C(\mathbf{x}) - \lambda C(\mathbf{x}) + s(\mathbf{x}) = 0 output dense numeric matrix — spatial field — defined tissue NA outside . single important parameter diffusion length: L=D/λL = \sqrt{D / \lambda} LL roughly radius influence one transcript. Set match biological scale interest.

title: Solver Guide: fd, green, and kde
text: fd method offers two solvers: "direct" (default): LU factorisation sparse matrix via Matrix::solve(). Exact fast grids ~400 x 400. Memory cost scales O(K1.5)O(K^{1.5}) K-cell system. "iterative": Red-black Successive -Relaxation (SOR). Converges within sor_tol sor_max_iter iterations. Lower peak memory; better large grids.  N = 128, two solvers agree high precision. direct solver typically faster . N = 512 , iterative SOR becomes competitive LU factorisation becomes expensive. SOR tuning: sor_omega = 1.7 safe default. Values closer 2 can accelerate convergence may cause divergence. sor_tol = 1e-6 sufficient visualisation. Tighten 1e-8 quantitative analysis. Increase sor_max_iter see convergence warning.
